newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks lock in solid gains by close.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks lock in solid gains by close.

text.p: *Stocks end with solid gains after Wall Street surges, Q1 inflation data digested. Volume 385.30 million, value A$768.78 million, 1,083 stocks traded, 307 steady, 483 up, 293 down.
A buoyant Australian share market locked in solid gains by the close on Wednesday after Wall Street surged and local markets comfortably digested March quarter inflation figures.
The All Ordinaries index climbed 24.7 points to 2,472.3.
June share price index futures added 28 points to 2,477, a 4.7 point premium to the index.

With a big rally in the Dow, stronger base metals prices and a consumer price index (CPI) that confirmed a low inflation environment, the market settled comfortably higher by noon and spent the rest of the day tethered to a narrow six point range.
"It looked solid all day after the States gave us the initial lead," said a dealer at a Sydney brokerage.
"CPI didn't cause much of a fuss. We finished off the highs but it was never going to hold it all."
Trade was strong with two-way business across the board the driving factor rather than interest in individual stocks.
"It has been a pretty quiet day even though turnover was healthy. There hasn't been anything that has been too enthralling," said dealer Scott Healey of brokerage Wilson HTM.
Aluminium producer Comalco was one feature, jumping 4.4 percent to A$6.70 after it forecast an improved 1997 result.

Macquarie Bank also caught the eye, leaping 5.5 percent to close at a record high A$9.60 as investors viewed the fees the investment bank was likely to earn from its role in the A$4.86 billion Loy Yang A power privatisation in Victoria.
West Australian regional Bankwest closed up one at A$2.53 after its full year net profit of A$94.5 million.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about eight to five, while about 28 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Options trade boomed ahead of Thursday's April series expiry, while the underlying market's strength generated heavy trade in the June SPI contract.
Turnover in June SPI contracts totalled 10,674 (5,697)

In other local markets, the Australian dollar shrugged off early tremors to edge higher as consumer price data confirmed inflation pressures were waning but not so far as to trigger another rates cut. By 4.40 p.m. (0640 GMT), the unit was up at US$0.7777/82 having slid as far as US$0.7745/50 just before the data hit dealing screens from an early US$0.7770/75.
Australian bond yields rebounded from their initial lows after a pretty benign March quarter inflation report was not weak enough for the market to rally further.
By 4.40 p.m. (0640 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.82 percent, steady with Tuesday's close.
